metadata.description: Wire format for `vibe registry mirror --json` (PROP-002 `#registry-mirror`): which versions of the source registry a run copied into the target `monorepo` / `localdir`, which it found unchanged, which it refused, and the commit it made. Source of truth for `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/registry_mirror_report.rs`.
False iff any version is an `alarm` (then nothing was written) or `unavailable` (the others were copied).
Always `"registry:mirror"` for this report.
The `[[registry]].name` mirrored from.
Its url (credentials redacted).
Where the source's version list came from.
The target: repository url (credentials redacted) and branch, a working copy, or a directory.
Every source version the filters selected, sorted by package then version.
Journal facts the run recorded in the target (a publication per copied version, plus carried-over yanks and tombstones); on a dry run, the facts it would record.
The target's registry index was rewritten (on a dry run: would be).
`monorepo`: a non-fast-forward rejection was absorbed by one refetch and retry.
`--keep-history`: history bundles written (or, on a dry run, that would be); 0 without the flag.
The commit made: pushed for a `monorepo`, local for a `working-copy`. Absent when nothing changed, on a dry run, for a `localdir`, and when an alarm stopped the run.

`index`: the source registry's package index (`primary.jsonl`); `layout`: a `monorepo` / `localdir` source's own tree and index; `tags`: the `v<version>` tags of the packages named by `--package` (a source without an index); `api`: the repositories the host's organisation listing names (`GET /orgs/<org>/repos` on GitHub or GitVerse), filtered to those whose name the registry's naming convention claims and that carry a `vibe.toml` with a `[package]` at a `v<version>` tag, each then read by its tags. Closed: a reader decides from it whether unchanged versions were compared by the source's recorded hash or by fetching.
`monorepo`: a repository url, cloned, committed and pushed; `working-copy`: a local Git working copy, committed into and not pushed; `localdir`: a directory registry, written in place.

`copied`: new in the target (on a dry run: would be); `updated`: a snapshot version whose content moved at the source, replaced because `--update-snapshots` was given; `unchanged`: the target already holds the same content; `snapshot-differs`: a snapshot version whose content moved at the source, left as it is (pass `--update-snapshots`); `alarm`: a frozen version whose content differs, or bytes that disagree with the source's own index — refused, and the whole run with it; `unavailable`: the source could not serve the version (its repository or tag is missing or denied) — the others are still copied and the run exits non-zero. Closed: automation decides from it whether the target changed and whether to page someone.
`<group>/<name>`.
The version is frozen (at the source or in the target): its bytes may never change.
The source withdrew the version; the fact is carried into the target's journal.
The content hash the source records (or, without an index, the fetched tree's).
The source ref the bytes were read at (a tag, or a monorepo branch).
The source commit, recorded in the target as the version's provenance.
Why a version is `snapshot-differs`, `alarm` or `unavailable`.

The Git tree of the source commit. For a `copied` / `updated` version written by this run, the version directory's Git tree hash was checked equal to it before anything was committed (`tree_verified`).
True when this run wrote the version and checked its directory's Git tree hash equal to `tree`. Absent when nothing was written or the source is not Git (a layout source).
